issues.description: Blocking read with no timeout or liveness check can hang the parent if the writer wedges
issues.detail: After stripping O_NONBLOCK, the inner loop calls os.read() with no poll, no timeout, and no process-exit check. If the subprocess stalls mid-write or crashes after partial output without closing the fd cleanly, the parent hangs indefinitely. The original poll loop existed for liveness; bound the blocking drain with a deadline or periodic check_process_exited.

issues.description: fcntl O_NONBLOCK flip mutates a shared fd in place with no restore and no return-value check
issues.detail: F_SETFL changes blocking mode on the fd and never restores it; if fcntl fails the flag is silently not cleared and the read loop spins returning partial content. Wrap the mode change in try/finally (or own the fd fully) and verify the syscall succeeded so a failure does not silently reintroduce truncation.

issues.description: Dead/vestigial branches (BlockingIOError handler, outer else: pass) left with stale comments
issues.detail: After the mode switch, BlockingIOError cannot be raised by the inner blocking read, and the outer else collapses to a bare pass with a multi-line comment about the old behavior. Either name the precise case each branch still covers in one line or delete them; right now they mislead future maintainers about what regressed.

issues.description: Removed check_process_exited fallback narrows coverage of abnormal-writer-exit cases
issues.detail: The deleted branch disambiguated 'process gone, pipe quiet' mid-stream, including macOS cases where read returns empty without EOF. The new code only consults check_process_exited when zero bytes ever arrived; a partial write followed by an abnormal crash may not return 0 from blocking read. Document or test this path explicitly.

issues.description: No regression test pins the >64KB multi-write race the patch claims to fix
issues.detail: The bug is an intermittent JSONDecodeError at ~86KB and the fix rests entirely on POSIX reasoning about blocking-mode EOF. Add a deterministic test that writes >64KB (pipe-buffer-sized) across multiple writes then closes, asserting full payload recovery. Without it the next refactor silently reintroduces the truncation.

issues.description: Unframed FIFO protocol is the root cause; read-side fix patches the symptom
issues.detail: One JSON document is sent over a byte stream with no length prefix, delimiter, or end marker, so 'where does the value end?' is answered by OS pipe semantics. A length-prefixed or newline-delimited frame would make EOF detection a non-problem and decouple correctness from POSIX blocking-read behavior. Worth a follow-up.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diagnosis is correct and the POSIX blocking-read insight is sound, but the implementation trades a truncation bug for a likely hang bug and ships without tests. Once O_NONBLOCK is stripped there is no timeout, no liveness check, and the fcntl flip mutates a shared fd with no restore or error check. Dead branches (BlockingIOError handler, outer else: pass) and the removed check_process_exited fallback narrow coverage of abnormal-writer-exit cases without documentation. Consensus verdict: NEEDS-WORK — keep the direction, bound the blocking drain, clean the vestigial structure, and add a >64KB multi-write regression test before landing.
